gbm_population_evidence.quote: Must have WHO Grade IV Glioblastoma or gliosarcoma based on histopathological OR molecular criteria

candidate_evidence.quote: Monoclonal antibodies, such as MBG453 and spartalizumab may interfere with the ability of tumor cells to grow and spread.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Trial of Anti-Tim-3 in Combination With Anti-PD-1 and SRS in Recurrent GBM

target_engagement_planned_evidence.quote: To assess the pharmacodynamic activity in tumor tissue and peripheral blood in treated subjects who undergo tumor biopsies as clinically indicated.

To assess the effects of MGB453, spartalizumab and their combination with SRS on immune cells in peripheral blood, including but not limited to the T cell compartments, myeloid cells, and serum proteins (cytokines and other immune modulators).

role_evidence.quote: Patients receive MBG453 and spartalizumab intravenously (IV) over 30 minutes each on Day 1.
Anti-Tim-3 in Combination With Anti-PD-1 and SRS

agents.drug_class_hint: investigational anti-TIM-3 monoclonal antibody (MBG453; likely sabatolimab)

role_evidence.quote: Patients receive MBG453 and spartalizumab intravenously (IV) over 30 minutes each on Day 1.
Anti-Tim-3 in Combination With Anti-PD-1 and SRS

coder_notes: Spartalizumab is registered only as an 'other name' of the MBG453 intervention but is clearly a separate antibody given to all patients; listed as its own agent. MGMT is mentioned only in prior-therapy history ('unless known MGMT promoter unmethylated'), not as an entry requirement or design biomarker, so no biomarker row. Exploratory immune/inflammation markers are not named specific tumour molecular biomarkers. SRS is radiotherapy, not an agent.
